memory_update.text: KLAC should remain the reference anchor for process control, inspection, metrology, reticle/mask, packaging, PCB, and yield-management exposure, but it should not dominate the discovery lane because it is already high-attention.

ONTO is a strong underfollowed-lane candidate for advanced-packaging inspection, 3D metrology, lithography, and factory analytics; next layer should verify advanced-packaging revenue mix and AI/HBM customer pull.

CAMT is a focused Nasdaq-listed advanced-packaging inspection/metrology supplier with apparent HBM and OSAT relevance; verify customer concentration, order durability, and whether demand is AI/HBM-specific.

FORM belongs in the adjacent chokepoint lane because HBM and advanced packaging increase known-good-die and wafer-test complexity; verify HBM probe-card revenue and recurrence before promoting beyond Layer 1.

This pass did not fully cover reticle-inspection pure plays, IC-substrate inspection suppliers, PCB inspection vendors, or yield-management software specialists. Later searches should test NVMI, AEIS, COHU, TER, VECO, ACLS, and non-U.S. listed niche vendors if allowed.

node: Semiconductor process control, inspection, metrology, reticle inspection, and yield management
summary: Expanded the process-control / inspection / metrology universe using a two-lane Serenity funnel. KLA remains the reference anchor because it directly spans wafers, reticles, ICs, packaging, PCBs, process control, and yield management. The underfollowed lane is stronger in adjacent advanced-packaging inspection, inline metrology, probe-card / wafer-test enablement, and factory analytics rather than in front-end reticle inspection alone. The best Layer 1B candidates for later verification are ONTO, CAMT, and FORM, with each tied to AI/HBM/advanced-packaging complexity through inspection, metrology, or probe-card constraints.
